entry.title: House in Ibiza, The Roca Views
entry.summary: An intervention conceived as a single 15-centimetre-thick plane that folds to follow the topography of an Ibiza hillside. This continuous gesture organizes a descending layout—from the entrance and garage to the living areas, pool, and bedrooms—framing sea views toward Clot d'en Llaudís and Punta del Puig Negre. entry.content:
Autor(es): FRAN SILVESTRE ARQUITECTOS

An intervention conceived as a single 15-centimetre-thick plane that folds to follow the topography of an Ibiza hillside. This continuous gesture organizes a descending layout—from the entrance and garage to the living areas, pool, and bedrooms—framing sea views toward Clot d'en Llaudís and Punta del Puig Negre. The design blurs the boundary between interior and exterior through shaded intermediate spaces, achieving a seamless integration with the natural landscape.

House in Ibiza, The Roca Views

Is it possible to build on a hillside by placing a single element? The house is conceived as a slender plane, just fifteen centimetres thick, that folds to follow the topography, organize the program and capture the landscape of Ibiza.

On this hillside in Ibiza, the project begins with the desire to intervene using a single element capable of adapting to the terrain. Rather than a fragmented composition of volumes, it proposes a plane just fifteen centimetres thick which, through a sequence of folds, follows the natural profile and responds to planning regulations. The section thus becomes the device that organizes the house and establishes its relationship with the site.

From the entrance level, the route descends through the house. The garage leads to the living area, then to the pool and finally to the bedrooms. Each part finds its place on the slope and is oriented differently to make the most of the site. This arrangement enhances both the frontal and lateral views, strengthening the connection between the interior spaces and the landscape.
his orientation opens the house towards the sea, framed between Clot d’en Llaudís and Punta del Puig Negre. The horizon unfolds continuously as you move through the house. We are interested in architecture’s ability to widen the field of vision and bring a landscape into view that changes with the viewer’s position.

The plane extends beyond the interior spaces to provide shade and protection from the sun, creating intermediate areas where it is difficult to define a precise boundary between the house and the outdoors. Seen from below, the structure recedes, leaving the slope legible. From within, it is experienced as a sequence of places open to the horizon. A single element folds to resolve the structure, the program and the relationship with the terrain. A sheltered place from which to enjoy Ibiza.

entry.title: Geo Balance
entry.summary:
Geo Balance is a playful exploration of shapes, colors, and balance, inspired by the stacking toys we used to play with as kids.
The project began with a series of sketches, experimenting with different geometric forms and compositions. I also explored different color combination through swatches to develop a palette that felt playful and cohesive. These ideas gradually evolved into 2D illustrations and 3D objects, where soft, fabric-like textures bring a tactile and playful quality to the shapes.

entry.title: El Capricho de Gaudí
entry.summary:
El Capricho, also known as Villa Quijano, is one of the few buildings Antoni Gaudí completed outside Catalonia. Built in Comillas between 1883 and 1885 for Máximo Díaz de Quijano, it is laid out to follow the sun from room to room, which earned it the nickname of the architectural sunflower.
Today it is run as a cultural space that welcomes thousands of visitors a month, from families and school groups to international tourists. Its image had not kept pace with that role. The brand needed to work across tickets, signage, workshops, merchandise, digital channels and the building's 140th anniversary, and it had to do so without ever competing with the building it represents.
The question was how to change the image of a Gaudí building, and who should be part of that decision.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Mubien ®

El Capricho, also known as Villa Quijano, is one of the few buildings Antoni Gaudí completed outside Catalonia. Built in Comillas between 1883 and 1885 for Máximo Díaz de Quijano, it is laid out to follow the sun from room to room, which earned it the nickname of the architectural sunflower. Today it is run as a cultural space that welcomes thousands of visitors a month, from families and school groups to international tourists. Its image had not kept pace with that role. The brand needed to work across tickets, signage, workshops, merchandise, digital channels and the building's 140th anniversary, and it had to do so without ever competing with the building it represents. The question was how to change the image of a Gaudí building, and who should be part of that decision.




El Capricho is one of the few buildings Antoni Gaudí completed outside Catalonia, a villa in Comillas laid out to follow the sun from room to room, which earned it the nickname of the architectural sunflower. Today it welcomes thousands of visitors a month, and its image had not kept pace. We began with a series of workshops with the El Capricho team to set the direction together, and from there built a complete brand, from strategy and verbal identity to the tagline “Una casa en clave de sol”, a house in the key of sun that also reads as treble clef in Spanish.

Every element comes from the building itself. With more than six thousand sunflowers on the façade, we drew hundreds more and used none of them: the symbol is taken from one of the house’s stained glass windows, a motif that reads as both sun and sunflower. The bands of tiles running across the brick became a musical stave that structures the layouts, the tile grid shaped the typography, and the palette follows the materials and how sunlight changes them through the day.

The identity extends to signage designed around how visitors move, a website built to make booking a ticket simple, motion and video, stationery, shop products and the building’s 140th anniversary.

Città di Ancona          Visual Identity / Environmental Graphics          2025

Ancona was born from geography: a promontory that bends into the sea, a natural feature that the ancients recognized and called "Ankón," the "elbow" of Italy. This singular curve, where the land embraces the sea, defines not only the morphology of the city, but also its cultural, economic, and symbolic identity. It is a shape that embodies both function and metaphor: shelter and openness, protection and horizon. 
Between its structures, both natural and constructed, there exists a constant tension: the sea that invites movement and the land that offers stability and tranquility. It is precisely from this relationship, between fluidity and permanence, between arrival and departure, between the gesture of the land and the force of the sea, that our proposed identity for the city of Ancona is born.

The challenge of the competition was not simply to design a logo: it was to conceive an identity system capable of translating the complexity of Ancona, a historic, vibrant, diverse city open to the world, into a contemporary language. The goal was to create a brand that was not merely a graphic symbol, but an institutional, cultural, and communicative tool, capable of representing the city's diversity while simultaneously offering unity and coherence.

Shortlisted proposal for the branding contest organised by Città di Ancona.

entry.title: GREEN VEINS — Iceland
entry.summary: Green Veins traces moss-filled drainage lines across Iceland’s volcanic highlands, where water, erosion, and sparse vegetation create luminous branching patterns that resemble a living network from above.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Jan Erik Waider

Green Veins traces moss-filled drainage lines across Iceland’s volcanic highlands, where water, erosion, and sparse vegetation create luminous branching patterns that resemble a living network from above.

GREEN VEINS – Highlands of Iceland

Across Iceland’s highlands, narrow drainage lines cut through dark volcanic terrain and fill with luminous green moss. Seen from above, these channels resemble a branching vascular system, tracing old paths of water across an otherwise sparse and often barren landscape. The contrast is striking: almost electric greens against muted brown and black surfaces, with every ridge and groove revealing how water has shaped the terrain.

What fascinated me most was this almost unnatural intensity of color. The neon green can look strangely artificial, even though it is entirely natural, which makes its presence within such raw and empty surroundings even more striking. These traces of moisture and vegetation turn an otherwise austere landscape into something almost organic, as if the terrain had briefly developed its own circulation system.

entry.title: Local Local
entry.summary:
Local Local is an urban inspiration hub with cultural consciousness.
A remotely controllable space rooted in the local area. It's a café, an art gallery, a blank canvas, a portal to the depths of one's thouts, a transit point to everything. We seek breakthroughs within reality, and opportunities within those breakthroughs. Local Local cherishes every moment of pause, capturing instances that transcend daily routines, and preparing for future moments of sudden inspiration. The only limit here is the prohibition against stopping your imagination. It's a space for every free spirit to enjoy a relaxed lifestyle that is true to the present, inspiring the now, and can be enjoyed anytime, anywhere. We aim to create an urban inspiration capsule with a sense of city environment awareness and cultural consciousness.
